In this study, we report the electrochemical deposition of PEDOT (HTM layer) directly on the MAPbI3 fi lm deposited on a FTO/TiO2 electrode and its implementation in a perovskite solar cell (PSC) with an n -i -p architecture (Scheme 1). The e ff ect of electrochemical post-treatments of the HTM layer on the performance of PSC has also been scrutinized.

The preparation of the FTO/TiO2/MAPbI3 architectures followed the Lewis base adduct method. 2 Briefly, the perovskite layers were prepared by the one-step method where all the precursors were dissolved in dimethylformamide and subsequently spin-coated onto the FTO/bl-TiO2/mp-TiO2 substrates. The initial studies were carried out on thin perovskite layers, which allowed in situ spectroelectrochemical monitoring of the PEDOT electrodeposition. To prepare thin perovskite layers, the spin coating solution consisted of 0.36 M PbI2, MAI, and DMSO. For the preparation of solar cells thicker perovskite layers were formed, from a 1.4 M PbI2, MAI, and DMSO containing solution.

unresolved_notes: The rapid, mild, and rapid-mild reduction arms change post-treatment conditions rather than the underlying functional-layer identities, so they were not split into separate device families. Their reported group-level conditions were rapid reduction at -0.6 V for 10 s, mild reduction at -0.5 V for 60 s, and rapid-mild reduction at -0.5 V for 20 s (span-5900167d697d, span-254915434424). Only the champion device is explicitly tied to one of these exact treatments.

The untreated and collectively post-treated qualitative photovoltaic outcomes apply to multiple devices, but no sample sizes or individual-device identities are reported. They are therefore retained as population-level statistics rather than individual-device performance observations.

Thin-MAPbI3 PSC architectures and MAPbI3/PEDOT specimens were used for in situ spectroelectrochemical, transient-absorption, SEM, Raman, or related characterization. Thickness alone does not define a new device family, and the supplied evidence does not report a photovoltaic performance outcome for an individually identified thin-layer device.

FTO/TiO2/MAPbI3 electrodes used for electrolyte exposure, electrochemical-bias stability, SEM, and XPS were partial stacks rather than complete photovoltaic devices, so their material-stability outcomes were not represented as photovoltaic StabilityTest records.
No scan direction was reported for the champion J-V curve.

The detailed precursor architecture FTO/bl-TiO2/mp-TiO2/MAPbI3 and the completed PEDOT-containing architecture FTO/TiO2/MAPbI3/PEDOT are both reported. The evidence supports the detailed ordered family architecture, but the source does not give one single verbatim stack string containing both the bl-TiO2/mp-TiO2 distinction and PEDOT.

Main Figure 2B and SI Figure S5 label Au above PEDOT in cross-section. The observed Au layer is retained with role not_reported; the figures do not establish its electrical function, thickness or deposition method. The text-only verbatim architecture still ends in PEDOT. The caption citations locate the images; the Au label was checked visually.
The regular-thickness MAPbI3 cells are described as a device configuration, not as a population statistic; no aggregate value or sample size is reported.
The preparation and assembly quantities in the supplementary methods are processing conditions already represented in family-01 and do not support new population statistics or device families.

The untreated and post-treated photovoltaic statements are group-level qualitative outcomes. They do not establish additional individual devices or permit attribution of those outcomes to device-01 beyond its reported 5.9% efficiency.
